kokoro.transcript: On June 8th, 2004, more than half the population of the world were treated to a rare astronomical event. For over six hours, the planet Venus steadily inched its way over the surface of the Sun. This transit of Venus was the first since December 6, 1882. On that occasion, the American astronomer Professor Simon Newcomb led a party to South Africa to observe the event. They were based at a girls' school, where, it is alleged, the combined forces of three schoolmistresses outperformed the professionals with the accuracy of their observations.
